about.intro_content: Prof. Xiang Guo is a Professor, Chief Physician and Doctoral Advisor in the Department of Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC), Guangzhou. He has specialised in the clinical diagnosis, combination therapy and surgical treatment of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) since 1995.
about.detailed_content: Prof. Guo's clinical work focuses on rescue and salvage surgery for recurrent or residual NPC, including minimally invasive and endoscopic approaches, as well as surgical management of complications following radiotherapy. He has authored or co-authored over 50 peer-reviewed papers and edited or co-authored several monographs on nasopharyngeal carcinoma, including serving as editor of a dedicated NPC textbook published by China Medical Science Press. His research has also examined biomarkers such as VEGF, EBV DNA and gene expression profiling in relation to NPC prognosis and metastasis.

faq.section_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Prof. Xiang Guo

items.question: Does Prof. Xiang Guo accept international patients?
items.answer: CancerFax can coordinate medical report review and consultation support for international patients seeking an opinion related to nasopharyngeal carcinoma surgery at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, subject to hospital availability and case acceptance.

items.question: What is Prof. Guo's area of specialisation?
items.answer: Prof. Guo specialises in the surgical treatment of nasopharyngeal carcinoma, particularly rescue and salvage surgery for recurrent or residual disease and management of post-radiotherapy complications.

items.question: How can I request a consultation or second opinion?
items.answer: Submit your medical reports through CancerFax. The CancerFax team reviews the documents, prepares the case for submission, and coordinates next steps with SYSUCC's International Medical Center, subject to availability.

items.question: Is surgery an option for recurrent nasopharyngeal carcinoma?
items.answer: For selected patients, salvage surgical techniques developed and practised by Prof. Guo's team may be an option for recurrent or residual NPC, though suitability depends on case-by-case surgical assessment.

items.question: Does Prof. Guo treat complications from prior radiotherapy?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Guo has extensive experience managing surgical complications and sequelae following radiotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma, including post-radiation necrosis.
